svg.title: Fig. 6 — A family of confocal Cassinian curves
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 6, page 8. Section: cassinian.

g.data-text: The axes and the two foci F1 and F2 on the X axis, at the distances ±a from O. Every curve of the family has the same foci; they differ in the constant k of the product PF1 · PF2 = k².
For k a little larger than a (here k = 1.23a) the curve is one oval around both foci with a waist at the Y axis (at the height √(k² − a²)). Compute points as in Fig. 9 and join them.
For a smaller k (here 1.115a) the waist is deeper.
For k = a the waist closes at O: the curve is the lemniscate of Bernoulli, a figure eight with its double point at O.
For k < a (here 0.95a) the curve splits into two ovals, one around each focus.
The inflection points of the two waisted curves (small circles) and the curve through all such points: the lemniscate r² = −a² cos 2θ, with its loops along the Y axis.
